lineage: Frank Frazetta's 'Death Dealer' (horned-helm rider silhouetted against sky, raised axe) is the stylistic ancestor of Darkwolf. Fire & Ice quotes it directly in shot_00029 (rider silhouetted on a mountaintop, backlit, arm raised). The Frazetta paintings are INSPIRATION-tier: they establish silhouette, posture, and menace, but are NOT the literal design and must be pruned from wired <Picture N> clip refs, or H3 drifts toward an armored knight on horseback (cuirass, eagle emblem, mount). The canonical design is the wolf-head hood worn by a human, per the production model sheet and the user's traits.
eye_color_open_question: RESOLVED by pixel probe (tools/pixel_probe.py). The canonical still-life design ref (darkwolf_mask_closeup.webp) eyes measure YELLOW: left eye 86% yellow-hue px (#b7b687), right eye 50% yellow + 20% green (#afae8f). But the actual FILM stills render the glow TEAL-CYAN: shot_01243 eye = 100% blue-cyan (#4eb6c2), shot_01229 similar (#37a6af). So the user's 'yellow eyes' note matches the design ref; the film's on-screen glow reads green/teal. Pick per use: yellow = design-sheet truth, teal-cyan = what appears in the movie. (VLM called film glow 'green'; pixel says cyan-leaning.)
head_open_question: Model sheet draws a full anthropomorphic wolf head; film stills read as a horned helmet or cat/wolf hood with eyes glowing through. User intent = a human wearing a wolf's head as hood/helmet, eyes looking through the wolf's. Canonical design should follow user intent, not the sheet's literal wolf head.
belt_open_question: User hypothesis 'girdle or corset for battle' — cross-check vision says WIDE GIRDLE/WAR BELT: broad dark band from lower ribcage to top of hips, fur-trimmed along the top edge, worn on a bare torso, with a loincloth hanging below. NOT a corset (no boning/lacing, does not shape the torso). User's 'bronze plates' NOT confirmed in any ref — instead the loincloth carries circular medallion/disc patches. Pixel-structure on the line-art model sheet and the messy multi-panel ComfyUI_00020 sheet is unreliable; to measure belt height/plates precisely, need one clean full-body COLORED render.
